sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At the heart of Dots & Boxes is the simple yet addictive gameplay. Players take turns drawing lines between adjacent dots, with the goal of creating boxes. The first player to complete a box earns the right to color it, and the player with the most boxes at the end of the game wins. Sounds simple, right? Well, it's precisely this simplicity that makes Dots & Boxes so addictive and challenging at the same time.

One of the key mechanics of the game is the concept of 'completing a box.' A box is considered complete when a player draws a line that connects two adjacent dots, forming a closed shape. The player who completes a box earns the right to color it, and the color can be used to their advantage in future turns. For example, a player may choose to color a box in a way that will block their opponent's potential moves or create opportunities for themselves.

Another important mechanic in the game is the concept of 'strategy.' Players need to think ahead and plan their moves carefully to maximize their chances of winning.
